```{r setup, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Title: Hurricane Closeread
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Description:
# This document is a closeread document visualizing the formation of hurricanes.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Details:
# - Uses the ibtracs dataset to visualize hurricane paths.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inputs:
# - ibtracs dataset (CSV file): Contains hurricane details including ID, 
#   year, wind speed, latitude, and longitude.
# - User-selected filters:
#   - Hurricane ID
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output:
# - Closead of specific hurricane path
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
```

```{r}
# import CSV file with read.csv()

# read-in only first 16 columns
ibtracs <- "../ibtracs.NA.csv"


# names of first 16 columns
col_names <- c(
  "SID",
  "SEASON",
  "NUMBER",
  "BASIN",
  "SUBBASIN",
  "NAME",
  "ISO_TIME",
  "NATURE",
  "LAT",
  "LON",
  "WMO_WIND",
  "WMO_PRES",
  "WMO_AGENCY",
  "TRACK_TYPE",
  "DIST2LAND",
  "LANDFALL"
)

# data-type of first 16 columns
col_types <- c(
  "character",
  "integer",
  "integer",
  "character",
  "character",
  "character",
  "character",
  "character",
  "double",
  "double",
  "integer",
  "integer",
  "character",
  "character",
  "integer",
  "integer"  
)


dat <- read.csv(
  file = ibtracs,
  colClasses = c(col_types, rep("NULL", 158)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
  # skip = 77876, # starting SEASON 1970
  na.strings = " ")

colnames(dat) <- col_names

# Extract date and time components
dat$DATE <- as.Date(dat$ISO_TIME)  # Date only
dat$DATETIME <- as.POSIXct(dat$ISO_TIME, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")  # Full date-time
dat$TIME <- format(as.POSIXct(dat$ISO_TIME, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "%H:%M:%S")  # Time only
dat$DATETIME <- ymd_hms(dat$ISO_TIME)
```

```{r}
# Define North Atlantic region limits
min_lon <- -100  # Western boundary
max_lon <- 0   # Eastern boundary
min_lat <- 0     # Southern boundary
max_lat <- 60    # Northern boundary
```

```{r}
# Set the hurricane ID (could also be user input)
#hurricane_id <- "2018280N18273"
#hurricane_id <- "2005217N13327"
hurricane_id <- "2005236N23285"  

# Filter for the selected hurricane
hurricane_track <- dat |> filter(SID == hurricane_id)

# Start point
hurricane_start <- hurricane_track |> slice(1) |> select(LON, LAT)

# Classify all points into categories
hurricane_track <- hurricane_track |> 
    mutate(category = case_when(
        WMO_WIND < 34 ~ "Tropical Depression",  
        WMO_WIND >= 34 & WMO_WIND < 64 ~ "Tropical Storm",
        WMO_WIND >= 64 & WMO_WIND < 83 ~ "Category 1",
        WMO_WIND >= 83 & WMO_WIND < 96 ~ "Category 2",
        WMO_WIND >= 96 & WMO_WIND < 113 ~ "Category 3",
        WMO_WIND >= 113 & WMO_WIND < 137 ~ "Category 4",
        WMO_WIND >= 137 ~ "Category 5"
    ))


# Helper to get first time for a category
find_first_datetime <- function(track, cat) {
    filtered <- track |> filter(category == cat)
    if (nrow(filtered) > 0) {
        return(filtered |> slice(1) |> pull(DATETIME))
    } else {
        return(NA)
    }
}

# Find times when the hurricane transitions into each category
date_ts <- find_first_datetime(hurricane_track, "Tropical Storm")
date_cat1 <- find_first_datetime(hurricane_track, "Category 1")
date_cat2 <- find_first_datetime(hurricane_track, "Category 2")
date_cat3 <- find_first_datetime(hurricane_track, "Category 3")
date_cat4 <- find_first_datetime(hurricane_track, "Category 4")
date_cat5 <- find_first_datetime(hurricane_track, "Category 5")

# Handle Category 5 drop-off (if it ever reaches Cat 5)
if (!is.na(date_cat5)) {
    first_drop_from_cat5 <- hurricane_track |> 
        filter(DATETIME > date_cat5 & WMO_WIND < 137) |> 
        slice(1)
    date_end_cat5 <- if (nrow(first_drop_from_cat5) > 0) first_drop_from_cat5$DATETIME else tail(hurricane_track$DATETIME, 1)
} else {
    date_end_cat5 <- NA
    after_cat5_landfall <- NA  # Ensuring it is defined to prevent errors
}


# Handle landfall after Cat 5 (if any)
# Ensure after_cat5_landfall always exists (even if empty)
after_cat5_landfall <- tibble(LON = numeric(), LAT = numeric(), DATETIME = as.POSIXct(character()))

if (!is.na(date_end_cat5)) {
    after_cat5_landfall <- hurricane_track |> 
        filter(DATETIME > date_end_cat5 & DIST2LAND == 0) |> 
        slice(1)
    date_landfall_after_cat5 <- if (nrow(after_cat5_landfall) > 0) after_cat5_landfall$DATETIME else NA
} else {
    date_landfall_after_cat5 <- NA
}

# Construct track segments — fully overlapping
hurricane_nothing <- hurricane_track |> filter(DATETIME <= date_ts)

hurricane_tropicalstorm <- hurricane_track |> 
    filter(DATETIME >= date_ts & DATETIME <= date_cat1)

hurricane_category1 <- hurricane_track |> 
    filter(DATETIME >= date_cat1 & DATETIME <= date_cat2)

hurricane_category2 <- hurricane_track |> 
    filter(DATETIME >= date_cat2 & DATETIME <= date_cat3)

hurricane_category3 <- hurricane_track |> 
    filter(DATETIME >= date_cat3 & DATETIME <= date_cat4)

hurricane_category4 <- hurricane_track |> 
    filter(DATETIME >= date_cat4 & DATETIME <= date_cat5)

hurricane_during_category5 <- hurricane_track |> 
    filter(DATETIME >= date_cat5 & DATETIME <= date_end_cat5)

# After Cat 5 until landfall
hurricane_after_cat5_until_landfall <- if (!is.na(date_landfall_after_cat5)) {
    hurricane_track |> filter(DATETIME >= date_end_cat5 & DATETIME <= date_landfall_after_cat5)
} else {
    hurricane_track |> filter(DATETIME >= date_end_cat5)  # if no landfall, this is the rest
}

# Final section after landfall (rest of track)
hurricane_rest_of_track <- if (!is.na(date_landfall_after_cat5)) {
    hurricane_track |> filter(DATETIME > date_landfall_after_cat5)
} else {
    tibble(LON = numeric(), LAT = numeric(), DATETIME = as.POSIXct(character()))
}

# Load world map
world_map <- ne_countries(returnclass = "sf")

hurricane_name <- str_to_title(unique(hurricane_track$NAME))
hurricane_year <- unique(hurricane_track$SEASON)
plot_title <- paste("Hurricane", hurricane_name, "(", hurricane_year, ")", sep = " ")

# Helper function to get the first date when a hurricane reaches a given category
find_first_date <- function(track, cat) {
    filtered <- track |> filter(category == cat)
    if (nrow(filtered) > 0) {
        return(format(filtered |> slice(1) |> pull(DATE), "%d/%m/%Y"))  # Format date as DD/MM/YYYY
    } else {
        return(NA)
    }
}

# Extract first appearance dates for each category
date_td <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Tropical Depression")  # New
date_ts <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Tropical Storm")
date_cat1 <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Category 1")
date_cat2 <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Category 2")
date_cat3 <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Category 3")
date_cat4 <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Category 4")
date_cat5 <- find_first_date(hurricane_track, "Category 5")

# Extract landfall date from after_cat5_landfall (if it exists)
date_landfall <- if (nrow(after_cat5_landfall) > 0) format(after_cat5_landfall$DATETIME[1], "%d/%m/%Y") else NA

# Extract wind speed at landfall
wind_at_landfall <- if (nrow(after_cat5_landfall) > 0) after_cat5_landfall$WMO_WIND[1] else NA

# Determine the hurricane category at landfall
category_at_landfall <- case_when(
    is.na(wind_at_landfall) ~ NA_character_,  # No landfall
    wind_at_landfall < 34 ~ "Tropical Depression",
    wind_at_landfall >= 34 & wind_at_landfall < 64 ~ "Tropical Storm",
    wind_at_landfall >= 64 & wind_at_landfall < 83 ~ "Category 1",
    wind_at_landfall >= 83 & wind_at_landfall < 96 ~ "Category 2",
    wind_at_landfall >= 96 & wind_at_landfall < 113 ~ "Category 3",
    wind_at_landfall >= 113 & wind_at_landfall < 137 ~ "Category 4",
    wind_at_landfall >= 137 ~ "Category 5"
)


```

This is the story of `r hurricane_name`.

  geom_point(data = hurricane_start, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), 
             color = "red", size = 3) +  # Starting point
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(min_lon, max_lon), ylim = c(min_lat, max_lat)) +  # Zoom to North Atlantic
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = plot_title,
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

# Ensure after_cat5_landfall is an empty tibble if no data
if (!exists("after_cat5_landfall") || is.null(after_cat5_landfall)) {
    after_cat5_landfall <- tibble(LON = numeric(), LAT = numeric(), DATETIME = as.POSIXct(character()))
}

# Create the ggplot object
p <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = world_map, fill = "#DCDCDC", color = "black") +
    geom_point(data = hurricane_start, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "gray", size = 3) +  
    geom_path(data = hurricane_nothing, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "gray", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_tropicalstorm, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#FFC0C0", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_category1, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#FFA0A0", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_category2, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#FF8080", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_category3, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#FF6060", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_category4, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#FF3030", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_during_category5, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#B00000", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_path(data = hurricane_after_cat5_until_landfall, aes(x = LON, y = LAT), color = "#FF3030", linewidth = 1.2) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(min_lon, max_lon), ylim = c(min_lat, max_lat)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

# Conditionally add geom_point() only if after_cat5_landfall has data
if (nrow(after_cat5_landfall) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_point(data = after_cat5_landfall, aes(LON, LAT), color = "#FF3030", size = 3)
}

# Print the plot
print(p)
